steps.name: Confused Individual
steps.text: Bells...? Why am I hearing them ring from all directions?
Her voice is so soft that it does not even echo off the walls.
Whenever the foggy light comes, lots of tiny holes appear in the walls, opening and closing, breathing. When the light disappears, the walls turn white and silent.

steps.name: Confused Individual
steps.text: That light... is very different from the Holy City's light that the Bishop talked about...

steps.name: Cold Voice
steps.text: (Unknown language) That light is a simulated F spectrum.

steps.name: Confused Individual
steps.text: I can hear you. How can I see you?
She presses her nails to the wall. It feels warm and soft, as if she's touching someone else's fingertips—
—so she places her whole palm against the wall, pressing closely to the wall's fine patterns and textures.
Wherever her hand moves, the patterns stretch along with it, as if they're quietly guiding her by the hand.

steps.name: Confused Individual
steps.text: You're... responding to me?
She runs forward for a bit, and the wall extends with her, leading her.

steps.name: Confused Individual
steps.text: There are so many doors and so many different paths here. Where do they all lead?
The Cautus stops walking. She sees a 'god' standing in midair, a short distance in front of her. Its silhouette is massive.

The surface of the god's body carries a murky sheen, unlike that of any metal. It nimbly arranges a vast array of glowing fragments into patterns. As the patterns change, the fragments shift color in turn.
But the girl notices that there is no halo on the 'god's' head. The midair colossus completely ignores her, gliding past without hesitation.
Another similar being approaches and stops in front of her.
It seems to be asking her a question.

steps.name: Confused Individual
steps.text: I don't understand what you're saying.
The 'god' is quiet for a moment. Then it switches from its own language to another one and continues talking.

steps.name: Mechanical Lifeform
steps.text: (Unknown language) Your use of language is primitive.
The 'god' extends its supple limbs to cover the Cautus's head. The Cautus nervously shuts her eyes.

steps.name: Mechanical Lifeform
steps.text: (Unknown language) There's no need to fear. I am analyzing your brain frequency and will upload it to Anseta.

steps.name: Mechanical Lifeform
steps.text: Language. You. Sufficient to communicate.

steps.name: Mechanical Lifeform
steps.text: ...Not yet vectorized, extrapolation, deduction. Language, temporary adjustment. Resonance, necessary.

steps.name: Confused Individual
steps.text: I... can't understand you. Can you understand me?

steps.name: Mechanical Lifeform
steps.text: Indubitably.

steps.name: Confused Individual
steps.text: —Then are you... God?
The Cautus nervously asks the question that she is most desperate for an answer to.

steps.name: Mechanical Lifeform
steps.text: 'God', question. Definition, necessary.

steps.name: Confused Individual
steps.text: The Bishop says that God is the embodiment of the Law and the Lord of the Holy City, who protects the sick and the dearly departed. But these things that he says were never recorded in the history books.

steps.name: Mechanical Lifeform
steps.text: Forsake, god.

steps.name: Mechanical Lifeform
steps.text: God, not, necessary.

steps.name: Confused Individual
steps.text: If you aren't God, then who rescued me? Why have I been brought here?

steps.name: Confused Individual
steps.text: Or is this Kingdom Come? Are you here to guide me into the Kingdom?

steps.name: Mechanical Lifeform
steps.text: Questions. Too many.

steps.name: Mechanical Lifeform
steps.text: Resonance, lacking. Communication, inefficient.

steps.name: Mechanical Lifeform
steps.text: Raydistorter. I.

steps.name: Mechanical Lifeform
steps.text: Partial answer. Show you.
The being who calls itself 'Raydistorter' uses its limbs to draw a window in the air and drag it to the nearest wall. The image in the porthole quickly fades from view.
A pale, eerie light wells up from nowhere, flooding the entire window. The image sharpens gradually—and the Cautus girl looks out the 'window'.
A shattered sphere floats in the dark expanse of space, dotted with countless stars. It is frozen at the moment of death.
All the pasts that have not had time to be told shatter into dust and are cast into the frozen void.
The dust particles find each other and circle around the former garden. They clump together into rings that float in the air.
The Cautus girl and Raydistorter 'sail' atop these dust rings into the dead silence.

steps.name: Raydistorter
steps.text: We see. Sail. Salvage.

steps.name: Raydistorter
steps.text: You, shudder. Fear?

steps.name: Confused Individual
steps.text: The faraway things, the twinkling things, they look like eyes. It's really scary.

steps.name: Confused Individual
steps.text: They're just stars, but they feel alien to me. There are too many of them; they are too close, too bright.

steps.name: Confused Individual
steps.text: You're not scared?

steps.name: Raydistorter
steps.text: Fear is unnecessary.

steps.name: Raydistorter
steps.text: Fear, too limiting, too inadequate, to describe.
The Cautus looks through the window and sees that tiny holes have appeared in the walls of the ship.
A white light appears somewhere far, far in the distance. It starts growing, and growing until it covers up almost the entire window.
The blinding light caresses the surface of the land of death, covering and hiding everything from any would-be watchful eyes.
The Cautus girl looks directly at the light, as a fear is continually invading her heart, a fear she does not understand.
It's the pale light of a dying star.
A dead planet still orbits the star, and the great ship clinging to the star ring must endure its light and its wailing, again and again, without end.

steps.name: Raydistorter
steps.text: See, yes?

steps.name: Raydistorter
steps.text: Only, grave. No, 'Holy City'.

steps.name: Raydistorter
steps.text: Only, cycles, only, laws. No... 'gods'.

steps.name: Raydistorter
steps.text: Universe. Welcome.

steps.name: Raydistorter
steps.text: You. Traveler. Name?

steps.name: Confused Individual
steps.text: Hierda.
'I don't know when it started, but the nickname the clerics used to tease me with became my name.'

a.text: Unlocking restricted-access project: PRTS Repaired Audio Log #0422
The dust has settled in Londinium, but hopes for peace in Victoria seem dim.
How much time do we have? I know you're listening, PRTS.
I need you to do everything you can to restore monitoring the Cradle Process, in the middle decks' under-development area.
And... prepare to grant Closure access to my permissions.
There's a lot left to do. How much will I manage myself?
Administrator, do you want to unlock the next classified log?
Three years after the Londinium incident

steps.name: 'Beepy'
steps.text: (Sliding quickly)

steps.name: 'Beepy'
steps.text: (Proudly claiming credit)

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Good work. It seems like Closure and Mechanist's upgrades were effective.

steps.name: 'Beepy'
steps.text: (Spins happily)

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Hey. The repair work on this sector is nearly complete.
She feels a small body make contact with her back, hugging her neck and giggling.
Alanna knows the giggle well. Sometimes, it makes her happy, and sometimes it makes her anxious.
She takes the girl she loves so much up on her back.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Potlid, I smell cream stew!

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Lanns, you're going to ruin the surprise!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: It smells too good! I couldn't help myself!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: You sure are happy. I guess the Doctor agreed?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Yes! I saw there was an opening for volunteer work in the Rim Billiton office, and I signed up as soon as I could.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: The food I cook now can't cure a miner's Oripathy, sure, but our Rhodes Islander friends can, and I can fill their stomachs.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: If Savage and Ray hadn't vouched for me, the Doctor might've rejected my application on the spot.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Well, it's my responsibility as your guardian to accompany you, obviously.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Savage and Ray are with me. No worries!

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: But even when I'm not around, you still have to eat right, Lanns. I've left a full week's worth of soups of the day in the kitchen—all your favorite flavors.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: My colleagues in Logistics will keep an eye on you for me.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Haha. You're the boss, Potlid.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: But will you really be able to stand leaving your friends?

steps.name: 'Beepy'
steps.text: (Exaggerated nod)

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Yes. The Beepy's also a good friend of mine.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: But lots of the people I know have applied to serve as backup in this place or that, and I'm not about to fall behind.

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Everyone's looking forward to touring our new home after the mission is over. Lanns, you promised me that Rhodes is gonna look even more beautiful once the renovations are done!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: (Shhh—Of course, I peeked at Closure's blueprints before.)

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: Also...

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Also?

steps.name: Warmy
steps.text: I was already brave enough to say goodbye to my family and set off on a long journey, just like my dad did. Lanns, you just wait for my return!

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: A giant cookie? Is this from Ceobe?

steps.name: Gummy
steps.text: Lots of operators getting ready to head out to support posts got cookies.

steps.name: Gummy
steps.text: 'You gotta eat good when you're traveling.' Kay was really firm with me on that.

steps.name: Gummy
steps.text: I just wonder if she's gonna end up eating most of the cookies before she gets to share them.

steps.name: Gummy
steps.text: I set it up with Vulcan to bake a batch of cookies as quickly as possible, so Kay could pass them out to all the operators going on field missions.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: When the time comes, I'll have Sonya go with Kay to distribute them.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Why—

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Forget it. I'll just drag Leto along with me.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Haha. I'm fine as long as you give me the honey drink you owe me once we get there.

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: With a drink in my hand, I'm at your command, General Zima!

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Gah. What a headache. All this talking-to-people shit... This is Natalya's work.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: But Rosa can't be everywhere at once—she has a lot of specific plans to go over with Amiya too, you know.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: This trip's going to be a bit more trouble than usual—after all, we're going to—

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: (In Ursine) Ursus.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Or did you give the task of planning with Amiya to Rosa because you were afraid you couldn't do it?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Who said I couldn't do it? It's just—
Ursus, the place they all left together.
So much time has passed since then. Zima believes they are ready to go back and face the place once more.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Gummy, what's wrong with your hand?

steps.name: Gummy
steps.text: N-Nothing, Zima. It's just a little sore, is all. We had them baking too many cookies. The bakers in the canteen got worn out.

steps.name: Gummy
steps.text: Even Kay, waiting right outside the door, had to get dragged in to help like a good girl.

steps.name: Gummy
steps.text: Don't worry about me, Zima. She wants to fill the bellies of the operators who took good care of her and are now leaving home. I feel the same way.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: We'll do our part as well.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Anyways, Natalya also needs to spend some time—
You need help? Count me in.

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: See, Little Cub? Look what I can whip up in the kitchen.

steps.name: Gummy
steps.text: Instructor Dur-nar?

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: The Doctor showed me your application. I took the liberty of applying to travel with you—as your 'guardian.'

steps.name: Dur-nar
steps.text: Truth is, the Doctor was too worried about sending you back. I'm worried enough myself.

steps.name: Gummy
steps.text: Zima...?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Welcome!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Rosa, the Doctor didn't want to approve your application, at first.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Medical assessed all of you and recommended that we be a bit more careful with your itinerary.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: But, in the end, the Doctor respected our wishes?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: That's because of Zima.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: She burst into the Doctor's office and vowed to protect you, promising your safe return to Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Just like before.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: I kept them alive in Chernobog, I got us through it. This time's no different.

options: This isn't just about your safety.
This encounter with Ursus will be very different from before.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Natalya and I have it worked out—If we operate under her family's Rostov Industries, we'll have an easier time moving around.

options: I'm not worried about your status.
Rhodes Island has ways to deal with things like that.
The assessment says you aren't fully prepared yet.
There are other logistics tasks you can choose.
There are always other ways you can help Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: We're all nervous about going back, at least a bit. But we can't keep hiding from it.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: This isn't some 'journey home for self-healing.' We looked over the risks and volunteered because we think we're a good fit for operations in Ursus.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: We decided to call Rhodes Island our home a long time ago.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: So I can guarantee I'll bring them back home, safe and sound.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Sonya has always been braver than me.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Amiya, as far as the details of our collaboration with Rostov Industries, I'd appreciate it if Dr. Kal'tsit and the Doctor could take a closer look.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: I believe this will only be beneficial to our operations.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Consider it done, Rosa.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: However, I still recommend that you avoid conducting any operations in Chernobog for now.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Ursus is still patrolling the area as closely as ever, and your identities are still an issue.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: We'll stay in contact with the ship—there are still many aspects of the Ursine operation that will be up to you to assess.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Have a safe trip, Rosa.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: The ship will be sending additional Logistics and Medical staff to accompany you—not only to support your operation, but also to explore the possibility of establishing a permanent office in Ursus.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: By the way, someone else came to find me after your travel plans were announced. She hopes to join you on your journey.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Gummy
steps.text: (Stomach growling)

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Gummy, put the pot down. You eat your fill first!

steps.name: Gummy
steps.text: Huh? I haven't gone hungry in a very long time.

steps.name: Gummy
steps.text: (Stomach growling)

steps.name: Gummy
steps.text: Hehe. Maybe I was just too busy today and forgot to eat, Istina.

steps.name: Gummy
steps.text: You and Zima are here, so I'll be fine.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Then get to eating, you hear me?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Open wide, Gummy.

steps.name: Gummy
steps.text: Mm-mm, I'm full, Leto!

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: Come to think of it, do you have anything you need us to bring, Zima? Personal thingies? I brought some big crates with me.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Well, let's bring the guitar Natalya gave me. Don't want her asking about it later.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Anything else, just leave it at home. Not like we're never coming back.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Leto, didn't you say we weren't taking anything?

steps.name: Leto
steps.text: That reminds me—I've got some junk to give to someone. Mind if we swing by Kjerag on the way, Sonya?

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Should be fine. I'll submit my travel plan to the Doctor.

steps.name: Resolute Voice
steps.text: Excuse me, might I join you on your trip to Ursus?

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: Sorry, I know this request is sudden...

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: But I...

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: Sonya, let Zoya come with us.

steps.name: Rosa
steps.text: This rescue mission will be a long one. We can take care of each other along the way.

steps.name: Absinthe
steps.text: You already know, Natalya?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I talked to Rosa about it.

steps.name: Zima
steps.text: Haha. Don't sweat it, Zoya. This isn't our first joint trip.

steps.name: Istina
steps.text: Ceobe, wait, that cookie is still a bit raw in the middle!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: No! Stop her! She'll give herself a tummyache!

steps.name: Ceobe
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: 'Beepy'
steps.text: (Politely stops her)

steps.name: Ceobe
steps.text: I'm gonna be late!

steps.name: 'Beepy'
steps.text: (Spins angrily)
Kay made so many cookies.
Those cookies should go to very, very good people.
Lots of wonderful people are setting out on a journey. They took good care of Kay at home, so Kay wants to make sure they don't go hungry.
That's the deal.

steps.name: Folinic
steps.text: Doctor, the copy rooms on each floor have been packed with people these past few days.

steps.name: Folinic
steps.text: This round of field deployments, going out to so many different regions, is the perfect opportunity for us to pick up local souvenirs—the wishlists everyone's been making are long enough to start a whole Terran Expo.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: In the past, Closure has suggested that the Procurement Department make unified purchases for the operators, but I rejected the idea.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Let's keep the spirit of the tradition alive. Procurement will be sending out a notice soon regarding reimbursement.

steps.name: Folinic
steps.text: Do you need me to bring you back anything from my trip to Victoria?
Kal'tsit shakes her head. She looks at the cookies Folinic is holding with a bit of suspicion.

steps.name: Folinic
steps.text: Ceobe shoved these cookies at me just now.

steps.name: Folinic
steps.text: She just made a gigantic mess in the kitchen, and Amiya is still trying to help clean it up.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Poor Amiya.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Folinic, you're going to have your hands full on this trip to Victoria.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: In addition to recovering data from several offices in the ducal territories, you'll have to monitor Na Saoirsí and Reed.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You'll have to coordinate with all the different offices to provide her as much support as possible.

steps.name: Folinic
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Folinic
steps.text: And Londinium?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Let Heidi know that we are temporarily delaying our return to the ship for debriefing. Ever since Londinium's Parliament restored contact with the outside world, it has resumed collecting messages from the Core nations.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The intelligence network that Heidi has been cultivating is extremely important. This is also why I am sending you to provide support.

steps.name: Folinic
steps.text: So overall, things aren't really that great? I see. I'll pay close attention to all of this.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Folinic, you need to take it easier.

steps.name: Folinic
steps.text: Wha?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You have a habit of overloading yourself.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I saw your itinerary. You're stretching yourself too thin. I deleted a few of the tasks.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Try not to dwell on the things you fear—and don't try and force yourself to take control of them, either.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Folinic, I never expected you to be like your mother... or me.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I don't support encouraging those who have experienced suffering to forget the hatred and violence they've endured. If we want to build a better future, we mustn't surrender.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Try to slow down your pace a bit, Folinic. Wanting to have more control over your life is good, but getting all anxious about it is just tantamount to self-torture.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It's a long road to Victoria, but I need you to remember the smile you had when you first walked in this room.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: This is my one and only requirement for you.

steps.name: Folinic
steps.text: I will remember that.

steps.name: Folinic
steps.text: I'll pick out a souvenir for you myself when I get to Victoria.

steps.name: Folinic
steps.text: Farewell, Dr. Kal'tsit.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Red, you don't need to hide.

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: I was afraid you would be angry.

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: You told me not to be sad about Siracusa... but I made you sad.

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: I don't want to leave Rhodes Island this time. I'm afraid you will force me.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I haven't prepared the transfer order for S.W.E.E.P. yet, Red.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Stay here on standby. Ascalon's orders will arrive soon.

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: After we receive the orders, can I stay by your side?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Yes. Didn't you arrive some time ago?

steps.name: Projekt Red
steps.text: Yes. I arrived a while ago.

steps.name: Savage
steps.text: Aunt Jemma and Mum prepared these canned golden radishes for me to hand out to my colleagues.

steps.name: Savage
steps.text: Sorry. There might be a few too many of them. Should we maybe store them in the kitchen first?

options: There's a veritable mountain of cans here.

steps.name: Savage
steps.text: I'll leave them with you.

steps.name: Savage
steps.text: All this stuff happened all of a sudden. It's been too long since I've been home. Mum's stockpile of canned goods is getting out of control. She just keeps dumping them on me over and over.

options: Didn't you just tell me they were prepared specifically for our colleagues?

steps.name: Savage
steps.text: Gah... Yes. Right.

steps.name: Savage
steps.text: Anyways, they're all mine. I'll decide how they're used.

steps.name: Savage
steps.text: Doctor, might I trouble you to help me distribute these to our colleagues, when you see them? Warmy's on a tight schedule, so I don't have time to do it myself.

steps.name: Savage
steps.text: Oh, right. The two cans with names on them... I saved them for you and Amiya. Don't give them out by mistake!

options: They look more or less the same.

steps.name: Savage
steps.text: —You... Of course they're not the same!

steps.name: Savage
steps.text: Oh right. I'll also need to take thirty cans on my own trip.

steps.name: Savage
steps.text: No. As gifts.

steps.name: Savage
steps.text: Warmy and Ray have an old friend, Jerry. Ever since he married Keira, his career has really taken off.

steps.name: Savage
steps.text: I saw the last photo he sent. His family has been blessed with quite a litter of kids lately. Warmy made plans with us to stop and visit them on the way.

steps.name: Savage
steps.text: And we haven't really changed much, eh? Well, Amiya sure does seem like she's matured a lot, ever since she returned from Kazdel.

options: Please take good care of Warmy and Ray.
Please take care of yourself as well.

steps.name: Savage
steps.text: I'm well aware of the situation in Rim Billiton. I'll make sure they're cared for.

steps.name: Savage
steps.text: Don't worry, Doctor.

steps.name: Savage
steps.text: I look forward to seeing you again after the field missions are complete.

steps.name: Savage
steps.text: Still, this field assignment covers a pretty wide area—I'm afraid it'll be quite a while before I can sleep soundly in my own bed again.

options: Don't worry. Rhodes Island will wait for you to return.

steps.name: Savage
steps.text: Righto!

steps.name: Savage
steps.text: Keep the lights on for me, Doctor.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Hey. What are you still doing here?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I just thought of something. We still haven't been given our medicine/health maintenance manuals yet. We need this guidance so that we can remember our health regimens.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I mean, this is going to be a long trip abroad. Will we all remember to eat our meals and take our medicines?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: The medic operators will take care of all that. Why are you worried about it?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: But we often do forget to take proper care of ourselves. You yourself, Lava, don't you forget to take your food rations with you, sometimes?

spans.text: forget to take proper care of ourselves. You yourself, Lava, don't you forget to take your food rations with you, sometimes?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: I... uhh... meh... whatever.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Then there's the other members of A1. The squad is going to be taking on some dangerous tasks. Kroos has to go on a long trip all by herself. Will they be okay?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Ugh... Enough already! Will you quit treating them like children?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: We've been at this for so long. We're all adults already!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I know... I get it...

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: It's just that—leaving a place I've spent so many years with everyone, day in and day out… and not knowing when I'll be back—it's a lot to take in.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I just feel a bit... empty inside.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Don't worry. We'll be back.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Rhodes Island is dealing with some stuff right now. I trust the Doctor, Dr. Kal'tsit, and Amiya can handle it all.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: All we have to do is complete our own tasks and be patient.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Rhodes Island is our home, and we're not gonna lose our home. No matter what happens, we'll be back.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Someday.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Right...

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: We'll be together again.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Your body temp hasn't come down. It seems like the old cocktail of drugs is no longer effective.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: However, your metabolic rate has not been impacted too much. After the concentration of the old drugs in your bloodstream goes down, I'll administer some new medications.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: These new drugs will decrease your pain threshold, but don't worry, I'll up your pain meds.

steps.name: Calm Infected
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Calm Infected
steps.text: There are a few new empty beds?

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: They left yesterday. Don't worry. They've just been transferred elsewhere for more targeted temporary treatment.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: By the way, a few people left some notes for you. They're in your bedside drawer.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Your condition is rather unusual, and we should keep you in a controlled treatment environment. Staying here with me under my observation is the best option.

steps.name: Calm Infected
steps.text: Okay. Thank you.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: What are you looking at, Chloe?

steps.name: Chloe
steps.text: There are little circles on the ceiling that keep spinning. Looking at them makes me feel safe.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: The crystals are still interfering with your vision. My next surgery will be an attempt to remove the crystals near your retinas.

steps.name: Chloe
steps.text: Every time I stare at them, they look like they've crept just a bit closer. It's like they're talking to me.

steps.name: Chloe
steps.text: Can you hear them?

steps.name: Chloe
steps.text: (Closes eyes) Their sound... it's like that old bell I used to hear.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: You mean the one you told me about before? From the bell tower in your hometown?

steps.name: Chloe
steps.text: There's more than just one bell tower. I was on a quest to repair all of them, and had already repaired quite a few... when they were all destroyed by cannon fire.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: I reached out to the operators we've got in Victoria—they looked into it for you. The town's been rebuilt, and the locals even repaired that old bell.

steps.name: Chloe
steps.text: That's great news! Now that the bell's tolling again, life can continue on. Quite a relief, isn't it?
Warfarin double-checks the instrument readings one last time, then injects the prepared medicine into the IV system.
The buzzing of the instruments mixes together with the noise of the IV system and Chloe's occasional gasps of pain.

steps.name: Chloe
steps.text: Dr. Warfarin, how many different types of medicine have we tried over the last three years?

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Let me worry about that. All your vital indicators have stabilized. That's what's really important here.

steps.name: Chloe
steps.text: Before I contracted Oripathy, I often cared for infected soldiers in the bell tower. I know exactly what it means when the crystals start spreading across your skin.
Chloe tries to move the muscles in her face, but the tiny spikes embedded in her skin twist her expression. Her wounds split open, and bright beads of blood begin to seep out.

steps.name: Chloe
steps.text: (Wry smile) You see? They won't even let me smile.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: As a doctor, I cannot guarantee outcomes. I can only promise that every medic in Rhodes Island will provide you the best possible care.

steps.name: Chloe
steps.text: Thank you, Dr. Warfarin.

steps.name: Chloe
steps.text: I just... miss my hometown.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: This report, it—!

steps.name: Touch
steps.text: The first time I saw this patient's charts, I thought there was some kind of error in the data then too.

steps.name: Touch
steps.text: But we checked the data several times, and it was correct.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: By all logic, no patient with this high a Cell-Originium Assimilation rate should still show any signs of life.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: It goes against everything we know about Oripathy.

steps.name: Touch
steps.text: And yet, the Originium is keeping the patient alive, in a way no one could have predicted.

steps.name: Touch
steps.text: Some of her internal organs have completely crystallized, but they're actually functioning more efficiently and stably than those of previous patients we've seen.

steps.name: Touch
steps.text: I haven't figured out what's causing this condition yet, but based on the data—the more her infection progresses, the healthier she seems… and the more pain she's in.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: We've never seen a case like this before. This may be some kind of new mutated form of Oripathy. If we can make some sort of medical breakthrough while administering her treatment...

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Maybe these people we rescued from Victoria really can bring a few miracles to Rhodes Island.
